long_biography.plain_text:
Backing BioNTech placed Thomas Strüngmann and his twin, Andreas, among the German biotechnology company's earliest major investors. Thomas brought commercial training and external relationship-building, while Andreas supplied medical expertise and internal scrutiny. Their division of labour paired business development with scientific assessment.

The brothers now direct their investments through ATHOS, a family office focused on pharmaceuticals and life sciences. Its holding company retains de facto control of BioNTech, combining long-term ownership with sector-specialist capital. They also founded the Ernst Strüngmann Institute for Neuroscience in memory of their father; the family foundation finances its research in cooperation with the Max Planck Society.
